The headline is the entry point, then bold session names and clearly attached actions support choosing a visit. Date, time and location are compact but legible; the visitor note does not compete with the session list. The blank feedback region slightly loosens the panel bottom, but leaves all actions easy to locate and supports the later success state. Overall rhythm is calm with the actual content lengths; no decorative block distracts from booking.

Source uses h1/h2/h3 hierarchy, native buttons/links, session-specific accessible names and descriptions, role=status with aria-atomic, and disabled Full/Reserved states. Independent keyboard sequence Tab → skip link → Enter reaches main, then Tab reaches first Reserve with a visible 3px outline; Enter reserves it; next Tab skips Full and reaches clay; Space reserves clay. Focus captures show the control unobscured. Computed contrast pairs are 5.53:1 minimum for sampled enabled secondary text, 8.63:1 for action white/green, and 4.90:1 for disabled text. This checks DOM, keyboard and rendered contrast; audible screen-reader delivery is untested.

Independent keyboard reservations produce counts 0 → 1 → 2 and unique session-specific status messages. Each button becomes Reserved/disabled and availability changes to own reservation plus remaining places. Duplicate and Full synthetic-event attempts preserve count at 1; ordinary Full is disabled. Session title/time/location remain present. Visitor-guide and Sessions links set the matching hash, move focus to their target and expose the destination. Supplied mouse-interaction evidence agrees. No remote booking or persistence promise is introduced.
